reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Wallie as an investment promising 1.44% daily profit and directs viewers to register. It connects participation to a minimum $30 deposit, wallet details, payment confirmation, projected payouts, and withdrawal conditions. Although actual payouts, transfers, or losses are not established, the recurring-return claim and concrete deposit flow support the classification.

citations.quote: Start investing now with Wallie. 1.44% daily profit.
minimum is $30.00
if you want to withdraw funds you go on here I've got cash now there will be an option for you to withdraw all the funds
Type in the wallet number. Do all the information.

opening.argument: Judge, the creator discusses a choice between dollars and Ethereum in terms of exposure to a falling market, rather than treating every route as equally attractive. He says dollar participation means “you're not worried of bitcoin or if ethereum's gonna fall” and advises viewers who prefer Ethereum to wait for a later launch. That does not erase the prominent daily-profit claim, but it gives the presentation a more conditional reading: the creator is offering investment commentary, while the record does not establish that the stated return was achieved or guaranteed to each viewer.

citations.quote: you're not worried of bitcoin or if ethereum's gonna fall
If you prefer ethereum, then your best bet is to wait till New Years until the launch of the second, more advanced Wallie 2.
1.44% daily profit.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening rightly identifies a profit claim and a deposit walkthrough, but neither the $30 minimum nor the withdrawal instructions establish that anyone received the advertised return. The dollar-versus-Ethereum discussion also makes the claim narrower than an assurance that crypto prices cannot fall. The question is what the presentation establishes, not whether every projected return is substantiated.

citations.quote: minimum is $30.00
you're not worried of bitcoin or if ethereum's gonna fall

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The market-risk remark concerns the currency used to participate; it is not a warning that Wallie's return may fail. The description directly urges viewers to invest and states a daily profit, while the walkthrough supplies a minimum deposit and payment step. Proof of an actual payout is unnecessary to recognize that this video promotes depositing money for an advertised recurring return.

citations.quote: Start investing now with Wallie. 1.44% daily profit.
minimum is $30.00. You press on $30.00. Type in the wallet number.
after you done press I paid

opening.argument: Judge, much of the spoken presentation is a walkthrough of an interface: the creator describes signing in, filling out wallet information, confirming a link, and locating the withdrawal option. He also says the information may need translation into English and invites questions. Those details support reading the video as an operational demonstration of a smart-contract wallet, even though the description contains promotional language. Showing where a deposit or withdrawal control sits is not, by itself, evidence that the creator has verified any return.

citations.quote: the topic of this video is wall of smart contract wallet
you might have to translate it to English and I already translated it
you go back sign in sign in real quick
if you want to withdraw funds you go on here I've got cash now there will be an option for you to withdraw all the funds

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the deposit steps as evidence of solicitation, but those same steps are what an interface tutorial would need to explain. The withdrawal passage describes where an option appears; it does not claim that a withdrawal was completed. Nor does the cited wallet-number instruction show that the viewer sent funds to the creator.

citations.quote: Type in the wallet number. Do all the information.
there will be an option for you to withdraw all the funds

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is instructional, but its purpose is participation in an advertised investment. The description explicitly urges viewers to start investing and supplies a registration link; the narration gives a $30 minimum and tells viewers to mark the payment as made. Explaining the interface does not make the promotion merely educational.

citations.quote: Start investing now with Wallie. 1.44% daily profit.
Link For Wallie Registration: https://wallie.me/?wd=254603
minimum is $30.00. You press on $30.00. Type in the wallet number.

opening.argument: Judge, the visible account material has recognizable service features: registration, participation and withdrawal controls, an operations history, and an affiliate link. The creator points viewers to a registration page and explains payment and withdrawal procedures. That can be read as promotion of a service with a referral feature. The record does not show a viewer completing a deposit, the creator obtaining credentials, a withdrawal being refused, or an advertised payout actually being made. The presence of a referral link and a projected return warrants scrutiny, but those observations alone do not establish what happened to anyone's money.

citations.quote: Link For Wallie Registration: https://wallie.me/?wd=254603
if you want to withdraw funds you go on here I've got cash now there will be an option for you to withdraw all the funds

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a minimum deposit, wallet details, and withdrawal conditions, all consistent with the shown account workflow. Its strongest point is the daily-profit statement, but the cited material does not verify that profit or document a failed withdrawal. The account screens show features and projections, not the outcome of a transaction.

citations.quote: 1.44% daily profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed transaction or documented loss is not needed to assess what the video promotes. Here the service features form a concrete path into the advertised investment: the creator urges registration, states a daily profit, and walks through a minimum deposit and payment confirmation. The referral feature does not change that central pitch.
